sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on the above, the completion of receiving the Torah depends on actual self-sacrifice, because the union of upper and lower requires nullification in both realms, and self-sacrifice in actuality involves the body and animal soul.

translations.translation: And 4)
And based on all the above, we can explain the reason that the completion of receiving the Torah
(And the Jews accepted)
depends on self-sacrifice (mesirut nefesh),
for the union of the upper ones and lower ones is through the nullification of the boundaries and existence of upper and lower
(as above),
and therefore,
in order for there to be the perfection of receiving the Torah,
the nullification of self-sacrifice was necessary.

And even though at the time of the giving of the Torah, when they said "We will do and we will hear," they accepted upon themselves to do all that they would be commanded, even if it would require self-sacrifice for this,
nevertheless, as long as the self-sacrifice is potential, it is from the aspect of the soul and is not in the body,
and since the nullification
(through which the union of upper and lower is effected)
must be both in the upper and in the lower,
therefore the perfection of receiving the Torah depends on actual self-sacrifice,
for actual self-sacrifice is
in the body and the animal soul.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This explains the superiority of the self-sacrifice of Purim over that of Chanukah, because in Purim the nullification was also from the body's perspective, as their bodies were utterly abandoned to destruction.

translations.translation: And based on this, one can also understand the superiority of the self-sacrifice of Purim over the self-sacrifice of Chanukah,
for even actual self-sacrifice is primarily from the aspect of the soul,
except that the self-sacrifice of the soul also affects the body and the animal soul,
and since the body and animal soul
(from the perspective of their essence)
are existence,
therefore the revelation of the giving of the Torah
(the union of upper and lower)
that is drawn into them through the nullification of self-sacrifice from the soul's side is something additional to them.
And this is the superiority of the self-sacrifice of Purim over the self-sacrifice of Chanukah,
for in Purim they were at the ultimate level of nullification
(and lowliness)
also from the body's perspective,
for they were completely abandoned to slaughter by anyone who wished,
and in the natural way there was no way to be saved from this.
[And even though the decree was only upon the Jews, and if they had denied [their faith] G-d forbid, nothing would have been done to them
(as brought above in section 1 from Midrash Tanchuma),
nevertheless,
since the decree at that time was not about fulfilling Torah and mitzvos but about the body,
to kill and destroy G-d forbid,
it follows
that their bodies were then at the ultimate level of lowliness.
For when the decree is about Torah and mitzvos
(as in Chanukah,
where the decree was to cause them to forget Your Torah and to make them transgress the statutes of Your will),
so that if one fulfills Torah and mitzvos they would kill him,
then,
the body
(from the perspective of its essence)
is not abandoned.
But when the decree is to kill and destroy G-d forbid, yet he has the possibility to be saved from the decree by denying [his faith] G-d forbid,
since the decree to kill him is
(not because he does not want to deny,
but rather)
upon the body,
it follows that the body
(from the perspective of its essence)
is abandoned.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Specifically through the self-sacrifice of Purim, the completion of receiving the Torah was achieved, because their nullification was also from the body's side, making them vessels for the revelation of the giving of the Torah in both soul and body.

translations.translation: And this is that specifically through the self-sacrifice of Purim there was the completion and perfection of receiving the Torah,
for through the fact that their nullification then was also from the body's side,
therefore they were vessels for the revelation of the giving of the Torah both from the soul's side and from the body's side.
And it can be said that this is also what is stated in the maamar, that at the time of the decree Israel was at the ultimate level of lowliness even in physicality,
for this hints at the reason that they were then vessels for the revelation of the giving of the Torah also from the body's side.
